title: Finite etale covers descend by henselian G-ring approximation
statement: Let $A$ be a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] (in particular Noetherian) and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $Y_0=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ its closed fibre (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]). Then for every finite etale $Y_0$-scheme $V\to Y_0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] there are a finite etale $Y$-scheme $U\to Y$ and an isomorphism of $Y_0$-schemes $U\times_YY_0\cong V$.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when (A, I) is a henselian pair and A is a Noetherian G-ring' (lines 1811-1840); it is the proof of Lemma 0A48 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian, line 1622, local Noetherian G-ring paragraph) with m replaced by I and Smoothing Lemma 0AH5 in place of Theorem 07QY

proof.text: Completion. Since $A$ is Noetherian, $I$ is finitely generated. Let $A^\wedge$ be the $I$-adic completion of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], $\iota:A\to A^\wedge$, and $\pi^\wedge:A^\wedge\to A/I$ the projection. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], $A^\wedge$ is $IA^\wedge$-adically complete and $\pi^\wedge$ induces an isomorphism of $A$-algebras $A^\wedge/IA^\wedge\cong A/I$ with $\pi^\wedge\circ\iota$ the quotient map $\pi:A\to A/I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $A^\wedge$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian], $(A^\wedge,IA^\wedge)$ is a henselian pair. Put $Y^\wedge=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A^\wedge$; it is proper over $\operatorname{Spec}A^\wedge$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Its closed fibre is $Y^\wedge_0=Y^\wedge\times_{A^\wedge}\operatorname{Spec}(A^\wedge/IA^\wedge)=Y\times_A\operatorname{Spec}(A^\wedge/IA^\wedge)$ (transitivity of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]), and the $A$-algebra isomorphism $A^\wedge/IA^\wedge\cong A/I$ gives an isomorphism $Y^\wedge_0\cong Y_0$ over $Y$.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when (A, I) is a henselian pair and A is a Noetherian G-ring' (lines 1811-1840); 'Observe that A^ is a Noetherian ring which is IA^-adically complete, see Algebra, Lemmas 031C and 0316' (lines 1815-1818); the henselian property of (A^, IA^), needed by the complete case as stated in the DAG, is More on Algebra, Lemma 0ALJ

proof.text: Complete case. Via $Y^\wedge_0\cong Y_0$ regard $V$ as a finite etale $Y^\wedge_0$-scheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting-complete] applied to the Noetherian $IA^\wedge$-adically complete henselian pair $(A^\wedge,IA^\wedge)$ and the proper $Y^\wedge\to\operatorname{Spec}A^\wedge$ (step 1), there are a finite etale $W^\wedge\to Y^\wedge$ and an isomorphism $W^\wedge\times_{Y^\wedge}Y^\wedge_0\cong V$ over $Y^\wedge_0\cong Y_0$.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when (A, I) is a henselian pair and A is a Noetherian G-ring' (lines 1811-1840); 'By the result above there exists a finite etale morphism V -> X^ whose special fibre is U_0' (line 1820)

proof.text: $A^\wedge$ as a limit of finite type $A$-algebras. For a finite subset $F\subseteq A^\wedge$ let $A_F\subseteq A^\wedge$ be the $A$-subalgebra generated by $F$; the $F$ are directed by inclusion, $A_F\subseteq A_{F'}$ for $F\subseteq F'$, and every element of $A^\wedge$ lies in some $A_F$, so $A^\wedge=\varinjlim_FA_F$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] with the inclusions $\iota_F:A_F\to A^\wedge$. Each $A_F$ is of finite type over the Noetherian ring $A$, hence of finite presentation (Hilbert basis theorem; Mathlib Algebra.FinitePresentation.of_finiteType). Hence $\operatorname{Spec}A^\wedge=\varprojlim_F\operatorname{Spec}A_F$ with affine transition morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit]. Put $Y_F=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A_F=Y_\emptyset\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_\emptyset}\operatorname{Spec}A_F$; then $Y^\wedge=\varprojlim_FY_F$ with affine transition morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit] (applied to $T=Y_\emptyset\to\operatorname{Spec}A_\emptyset$). Each $Y_F\to\operatorname{Spec}A_F$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence quasi-compact and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $Y_F$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $\operatorname{Spec}A_F$ being affine.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when (A, I) is a henselian pair and A is a Noetherian G-ring' (lines 1811-1840); 'Write A^ = colim A_i with A -> A_i of finite type' (line 1823)

proof.text: Descent of the cover to a finite stage. $W^\wedge\to Y^\wedge$ is finite, hence affine, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and etale, hence locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; so it is of finite presentation. By [thm-pd-spreading-out] (1), applied to the system $(Y_F)$ of step 3, there are $F_0$ and a morphism of finite presentation $W_{F_0}\to Y_{F_0}$ with $W_{F_0}\times_{Y_{F_0}}Y^\wedge\cong W^\wedge$ over $Y^\wedge$; $W_{F_0}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, being of finite presentation over the qcqs $Y_{F_0}$. For $F\supseteq F_0$ let $W_F=W_{F_0}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_{F_0}}\operatorname{Spec}A_F$, so $W_F\to Y_F$ is the base change of $W_{F_0}\to Y_{F_0}$ to the stage $\operatorname{Spec}A_F$ of the system $(\operatorname{Spec}A_F)_{F\supseteq F_0}$ (limit $\operatorname{Spec}A^\wedge$) and its base change to the limit is $W^\wedge\to Y^\wedge$, which is finite and etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite] (with $W_{F_0}\to Y_{F_0}$ locally of finite type) and [lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale] (with it locally of finite presentation) there are $F_1,F_2\supseteq F_0$ with $W_{F_1}\to Y_{F_1}$ finite and $W_{F_2}\to Y_{F_2}$ etale; for $F=F_1\cup F_2$, $W_F\to Y_F$ is a base change of both, hence finite and etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], and $W_F\times_{Y_F}Y^\wedge\cong W^\wedge$.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when (A, I) is a henselian pair and A is a Noetherian G-ring' (lines 1811-1840); 'By Limits, Lemma 01ZM there exists an i and a finitely presented morphism U_i -> X_{A_i} whose base change to X^ is V. After increasing i we may assume that U_i -> X_{A_i} is finite and etale (Limits, Lemmas 01ZO and 07RP)' (lines 1824-1829)

proof.text: Approximation. Write $F=\{\hat a_1,\ldots,\hat a_n\}$, so $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\to A_F$, $x_k\mapsto\hat a_k$, is surjective; its kernel is generated by finitely many $f_1,\ldots,f_m$ ($A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ is Noetherian), and $A_F=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. The inclusion $\iota_F$ says $f_j(\hat a_1,\ldots,\hat a_n)=0$ in $A^\wedge$. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-approximation] (with $N=1$; $(A,I)$ henselian, $A$ a G-ring) there are $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in A$ with $f_j(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=0$ and $\hat a_k-\iota(a_k)\in IA^\wedge$. Let $\sigma:A_F\to A$ be the $A$-algebra map $x_k\mapsto a_k$ (well defined since the $f_j$ vanish at $a$). Then $\pi\circ\sigma=\pi^\wedge\circ\iota_F=:\tau:A_F\to A/I$: both are $A$-algebra maps, and on the generators $\pi^\wedge(\hat a_k)-\pi(a_k)=\pi^\wedge(\hat a_k-\iota(a_k))=0$ because $\ker\pi^\wedge=IA^\wedge$ and $\pi^\wedge\circ\iota=\pi$ [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal].

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when (A, I) is a henselian pair and A is a Noetherian G-ring' (lines 1811-1840); 'Writing A_i = A[x_1,...,x_n]/(f_1,...,f_m) the ring map A_i -> A^ can be reinterpreted as a solution (a_1,...,a_n) in A^ ... By Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma 0AH5 we can approximate this solution (to order 11 for example) by a solution (b_1,...,b_n) in A. Translating back we find an A-algebra map A_i -> A which gives the same closed point as the original map A_i -> A^ (as 11 > 1)' (lines 1830-1837)

proof.text: The lift. Since $Y_F\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_F,\sigma}\operatorname{Spec}A=Y\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A_F\times_{A_F}\operatorname{Spec}A=Y$, the morphism $\operatorname{id}_Y\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma:Y\to Y_F$ is a base change of $\operatorname{Spec}\sigma$. Put $U=W_F\times_{Y_F}Y$. As a base change of the finite etale $W_F\to Y_F$ (step 4), $U\to Y$ is finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category].

source.place: Fundamental Groups, proof of Lemma 0GS2 (lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair, line 1749), paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when (A, I) is a henselian pair and A is a Noetherian G-ring' (lines 1811-1840); 'The base change U -> X of V -> X_{A_i} by this ring map will therefore be a finite etale morphism' (lines 1837-1839)

proof.text: Its closed fibre. The composite $Y_0\to Y\to Y_F$ is $\operatorname{id}_Y\times\operatorname{Spec}(\pi\circ\sigma)=\operatorname{id}_Y\times\operatorname{Spec}\tau:Y\times_A\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to Y\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A_F$, and the composite $Y^\wedge_0\to Y^\wedge\to Y_F$ is $\operatorname{id}_Y\times\operatorname{Spec}(\bar\pi^\wedge\circ\iota_F)$ with $\bar\pi^\wedge:A^\wedge\to A^\wedge/IA^\wedge$; under the isomorphism $Y^\wedge_0\cong Y_0$ of step 1, induced by $A^\wedge/IA^\wedge\cong A/I$ which carries $\bar\pi^\wedge$ to $\pi^\wedge$, this is again $\operatorname{id}_Y\times\operatorname{Spec}\tau$ (step 5). Pasting fibre squares [def-pc-fibre-product], $U\times_YY_0\cong W_F\times_{Y_F}Y_0$ and $W^\wedge\times_{Y^\wedge}Y^\wedge_0\cong(W_F\times_{Y_F}Y^\wedge)\times_{Y^\wedge}Y^\wedge_0\cong W_F\times_{Y_F}Y^\wedge_0$, both fibre products taken along the same morphism $Y_0\cong Y^\wedge_0\to Y_F$. Hence $U\times_YY_0\cong W^\wedge\times_{Y^\wedge}Y^\wedge_0\cong V$ as $Y_0$-schemes (step 2).

proof.text: Conclusion: $U\to Y$ is a finite etale $Y$-scheme (step 6) with an isomorphism of $Y_0$-schemes $U\times_YY_0\cong V$ (step 7), as claimed.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks pione.tex Lemma 0GS2 (paragraph for a henselian pair with A a Noetherian G-ring, lines 1811-1840), the parallel paragraph of Lemma 0A48, and Smoothing Lemma 0AH5. Made the statement precise (G-ring includes Noetherian; explicit closed fibre and Y_0-isomorphism) and removed lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-lifting-complete from stmt_deps (it is a proof dependency). Wrote the proof in 8 steps following Stacks: completion (A^ Noetherian, IA^-adically complete, henselian, A^/IA^ = A/I), complete case, A^ as directed union of finite type A-subalgebras A_F with Y^ = lim Y_F, descent of the cover to a finite etale W_F -> Y_F (Limits 01ZM via thm-pd-spreading-out, 01ZO, 07RP), approximation of the solution by 0AH5 with N=1 giving sigma: A_F -> A agreeing with A_F -> A^ modulo I, base change U = W_F x_{Y_F} Y, and identification of the closed fibre by pasting fibre squares. New nodes: def-weil-pbc-g-ring (unsplit), def-weil-pbc-adic-completion (Mathlib AdicCompletion), lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal (Mathlib, one lemma per clause), lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian (0316, unsplit), lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian (0ALJ, unsplit: Mathlib's IsAdicComplete.henselianRing is the root-lifting definition), lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite (01ZO, unsplit), lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-approximation (0AH5, unsplit). Tool uses outside the unit: thm-pd-spreading-out (sk-prop-jacobian-descent), lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change (sk-thm-br).

lean.statement: theorem exists_finiteEtale_lift_of_henselianPair_of_isGRing {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (hA : IsGRing A) (I : Ideal A) [HenselianRing A I] {Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsProper f] (V : (@IsFinite ⊓ @Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).Over ⊤ (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))))) : ∃ U : (@IsFinite ⊓ @Etale : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}).Over ⊤ Y, Nonempty (Over.mk (pullback.snd U.hom (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))))) ≅ Over.mk V.hom)
